l: Metal Forest, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: The Metal Forest is a huge dome containing glittering metal trees and masses of jewels. Queen Ann and the officers of Oogaboo enter it through a tunnel and remain trapped there until their situation changes.

l: secret tunnel (Metal Forest), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: The secret tunnel leading into the Metal Forest is lined with sharp, jagged rocks and is the most difficult of three secret passages. Queen Ann and the officers use it to escape, but it tears their clothing and bruises their bodies.

l: Ugly One's hut, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: The Ugly One's hut is a small shelter made of twigs and golden branches in the grove of natural trees. He hides inside it and initially refuses to come out, but later opens the door after making a mask.

l: Ruggedo's enchantment, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: Ruggedo's enchantment changes the Ugly One from a handsome man into an extremely ugly one. Kaliko does not know how to break it, and the Ugly One believes he must remain masked because of it.

l: freedom from the nomes, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: Kaliko grants the Ugly One freedom from the nomes after becoming the new Nome King. The Ugly One still fears accepting that freedom because he is ashamed of his altered appearance.

l: Ugly One's mask, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: The Ugly One's mask is made from Shaggy Man's red handkerchief with large white polka dots. It has holes for his eyes and nostrils and allows him to face the others without showing his features.

l: the officers' capture of Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-One
s: The officers of Oogaboo capture Ruggedo after discovering him in the Metal Forest. They believe he is still the Nome King, but release him when Files explains that Kaliko has replaced him.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Betsy, Shaggy Man, King Kaliko, Ruggedo, Polychrome, and their companions leave the Metal Forest after rescuing Shaggy Man's brother, the Ugly One. Ruggedo explains that one of three kinds of kisses might break the charm of ugliness, so Betsy, the Rose Princess, and Polychrome each kiss him in the dark passage. Only Polychrome's kiss, as a Fairy, restores Shaggy's brother's original appearance. The group then leaves the passage and prepares to return to the outside world.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Betsy learns about the Hotel Trees and Breakfast Trees in the natural forest and argues that Ruggedo should undo the ugliness he caused. She bravely kisses the Ugly One, then helps determine that her kiss did not break the charm and encourages Polychrome to try.

l: the Ugly One, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: The Ugly One explains that he has survived in the natural forest by eating Three-Course Nuts and breakfast nuts. After Polychrome kisses him, his transformation is reversed and he becomes Shaggy Man's brother again.

l: Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Shaggy Man rejoices at being reunited with his brother and anxiously asks whether the charm has been broken. After his brother is restored, he remarks that the man's recovered face is no more handsome than it ought to be.

l: Kaliko, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: King Kaliko leads the group back through the Metal Forest and toward the passage to the outer world. He permits Queen Ann and the Army officers to gather jewels and later helps Shaggy raise Ruggedo.

l: Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Ruggedo reaches the passage after losing many jewels from pockets that burst under their weight and admits that he no longer wants to be rich. He remembers that a special kiss may break the charm of ugliness, but he cannot initially recall which kind; he tests the results of the kisses by lighting matches and looking at the Ugly One.

l: Polychrome, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Polychrome offers to kiss the Ugly One because she is a Fairy and wants to reward Shaggy Man's unselfish affection for his brother. Her kiss breaks the charm and restores the Ugly One's original appearance.

l: Metal Forest, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: The group walks through the Metal Forest after the Ugly One is rescued. Queen Ann and the Army officers gather jewels there, while a trail of jewels leads from the forest through the passage because Ruggedo dropped them.

l: the secret passages to the Metal Forest, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: The passage leads from the Metal Forest to the outer world and is strewn with jewels that Ruggedo lost from his overloaded pockets. The passage is closed in darkness while the kisses are attempted, then opened to daylight after the charm is broken.

l: the enchantment of ugliness, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: The charm of ugliness was cast by Ruggedo on Shaggy Man's brother, transforming him from a handsome man into the Ugly One. It is finally broken by the kiss of a Fairy.

l: the kiss of a Mortal Maid, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Ruggedo recalls that the kiss of a Mortal Maid might break the charm of ugliness. Betsy, a Mortal Maid, kisses the Ugly One, but Ruggedo determines that her kiss does not break the charm.

l: the kiss of a Fairy, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: Ruggedo suggests that the kiss of a Fairy may be required to break the charm of ugliness. Polychrome gives this kiss, and it restores Shaggy Man's brother.

l: Shaggy Man's search for his lost brother, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Two
s: The rescue brings Shaggy Man's long-separated brother out of the Metal Forest and into the company of Shaggy Man, Betsy, King Kaliko, and the others. The rescue is completed when Polychrome's kiss removes the charm of ugliness and the group leaves the passage for the outside world.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Ruggedo follows the others back to the Nome King's royal cavern, where Betsy gives him food and asks Kaliko to let him stay. Ruggedo admits that he is sorry for his past behavior and promises to live harmlessly as a common nome, and Kaliko agrees to keep him if he behaves. Polychrome leaves the Nome Kingdom by riding a Rainbow back to her sisters in the sky. Betsy, Hank, Shaggy, and Shaggy's brother return sadly to the cavern after promising to remain together.

l: Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Ruggedo trails after the others to the royal cavern and humbly squats in a corner. After Betsy brings him food and drink, he says he is sorry for his past actions, claims he is harmless, and promises to behave so he can remain underground.

l: Kaliko, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Kaliko orders refreshments for the party and allows Ruggedo to stay in the Nome Kingdom as long as he behaves. He warns that he will drive Ruggedo out if the old nome acts badly again, as Tititi-Hoochoo commanded.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Betsy discovers Ruggedo hiding in a corner and softens toward him, bringing him food and drink. She asks Kaliko not to be hard on Ruggedo and later says goodbye sadly to Polychrome before returning to the cavern.

l: Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Shaggy is pleased that Ruggedo has reformed but hopes he will keep his word. He notices the Rainbow approaching and mourns Polychrome's departure, then reassures Betsy that he will never desert her.

l: Polychrome, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Polychrome realizes that she has finished helping her earth friends and longs to return to her sky home. When the Rainbow appears, she rides it to her sisters, calling goodbye and sending kisses to her companions.

l: the Nome Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: The Nome Kingdom remains the underground home of the nomes, where Ruggedo is permitted to stay under Kaliko's supervision. The companions return to it after Polychrome departs.

l: royal cavern (Nome King's cavern), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: The royal cavern is where the party reunites and receives refreshments from Kaliko. Ruggedo enters it cautiously and later joins the others there after Polychrome leaves.

l: Rainbow, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: The Rainbow descends to the mountainside and carries Polychrome away from the Nome Kingdom. It lifts her to the sky and melts into the clouds after she reaches her radiant sisters.

l: Ruggedo's reform, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Three
s: Ruggedo's reform is shown by his admission that he is sorry, his claim that he is harmless, and his promise to behave as a common nome. The others are pleased to hear that he has really reformed, though Betsy hopes he will keep his word.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Queen Ann abandons her attempt to conquer the world and wishes to return to Oogaboo, so Ozma has the Wizard transport Ann and her people home, along with the Rose Princess. Shaggy Man remains with Betsy Bobbin, Hank, and his newly recovered brother after Tik-Tok is returned to the Land of Oz. Ozma, Dorothy, the Wizard of Oz, and Tik-Tok decide that Shaggy Man's group should be admitted to Oz, and the Wizard magically transports them there. Dorothy eagerly goes to welcome Betsy, while Shaggy Man weeps with joy at being brought to Oz.

l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Queen Ann admits that she no longer wants to conquer the world and earnestly wishes to return to Oogaboo. Ozma has the Wizard transport her and her people back to their home.

l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Oogaboo is described as a corner of the Land of Oz and the home to which Queen Ann and her people wish to return. Ozma sends them back there.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Betsy Bobbin leaves the Nome King's cavern with Hank, Shaggy Man, and Shaggy Man's brother. The Wizard later transports her to the Land of Oz, where Dorothy eagerly goes to greet her and Ozma arranges rooms for her.

l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Hank leaves the Nome King's cavern with Betsy Bobbin and the others. The Wizard transports him to the Land of Oz, where Ozma plans a golden stall for him and hopes he will become friends with the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger.

l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Ozma uses the Wizard's magic to send Queen Ann and the people of Oogaboo back to their home. After learning that Shaggy Man will not return to Oz without his new companions, she decides to admit Shaggy Man, his brother, Betsy, and Hank to the Land of Oz.

l: the Wizard of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Wizard watches the adventurers with Ozma through the Magic Picture and uses magic to transport the people of Oogaboo and the Rose Princess home. He later performs another magical rite that transports Shaggy Man, his brother, Betsy, and Hank to Oz.

l: Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Shaggy Man finds his lost brother freed from Ruggedo's enchantment and remains with him, Betsy Bobbin, and Hank rather than returning alone to Oz. Ozma ultimately transports the group to the Land of Oz, where Shaggy Man cries tears of joy.

l: the Shaggy Man's brother, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Shaggy Man's brother is recovered from his long imprisonment by the Nome King and is freed from the enchantment of ugliness. Although he has no independent claim to a home in Oz, Ozma admits him so that Shaggy Man and the others can come there.

l: Tik-Tok, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Tik-Tok is transported back to Oz after serving Shaggy Man and his companions faithfully. He praises Betsy Bobbin and supports admitting Shaggy Man's brother because Shaggy Man is needed in Oz.

l: Dorothy, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Dorothy advises Ozma to admit Betsy and Hank to the Land of Oz and says that Shaggy Man's group should not be lost. She eagerly runs to welcome Betsy when the girl and Hank arrive in the palace.

l: the Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Land of Oz is said to include Oogaboo and to have a policy against admitting all mortals in distress, although several loyal mortals already live there. Ozma decides to admit Shaggy Man's brother, Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Hank.

l: the Magic Picture, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Magic Picture in Ozma's palace shows whatever scene Ozma wishes to see, with its figures moving as events occur. Ozma and the Wizard use it to observe the adventurers, and it later shows their disappearance when they are transported to Oz.

l: the Wizard's magic, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Wizard's magic can transport people over great distances and enables Ozma to send Queen Ann's party home. He uses pink powder, an incantation, a silver plate, and perfumed smoke to bring Shaggy Man's group to Oz.

l: the magic transport, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The magic transport sends the people of Oogaboo and the Rose Princess from the Nome King's cavern to Oogaboo without fuss or mystery. A second use of the transport brings Shaggy Man, his brother, Betsy Bobbin, and Hank to Oz.

l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world ends when Queen Ann changes her mind after suffering many hardships. Ozma sends the expedition back to Oogaboo.

l: the Land of Oz's admission policy, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The Land of Oz's admission policy treats admitting mortals as a serious matter and does not make Oz a refuge for every mortal in distress. Ozma makes an exception for Shaggy Man's brother so that Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Hank can also be welcomed.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Hank settles into Ozma's palace stable and discovers that he can speak in the Land of Oz. The Sawhorse, Cowardly Lion, and Hungry Tiger argue with Hank over which girl is sweetest, but Ozma teaches them that friendship matters more than rivalry and reconciles them. Dorothy discovers that Toto can speak words but prefers to communicate through barks and gestures. During a garden walk, Betsy Bobbin expresses her happiness in Oz and wishes that all children could live there.

l: the Sawhorse, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: The Sawhorse lives in a gold-paneled stall in Ozma's palace stable and is Ozma's favorite steed. He argues that Ozma is the sweetest girl, then accepts Hank as a friend after Ozma rebukes the animals.

l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Hank is given a stall and cushions in Ozma's palace stable and learns that he can speak after entering the Land of Oz. He proudly defends Betsy Bobbin as the sweetest girl and is reconciled with the Sawhorse, Hungry Tiger, and Cowardly Lion.

l: the Cowardly Lion, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: The Cowardly Lion rests in a cushioned room in Ozma's stable and insists that Dorothy is the sweetest girl in the world. After Ozma explains that friendship outranks rivalry, he accepts Hank as a friend and offers him help or advice.

l: the Hungry Tiger, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: The Hungry Tiger lives in Ozma's stable and watches Hank with interest. He supports the Cowardly Lion's defense of Dorothy, then rubs noses with Hank and becomes reconciled with him.

l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Ozma welcomes Betsy and Hank to the Land of Oz and explains that friendship is more important than rivalry. She reconciles Hank with the other animals and reveals that the spell of Oz affects animals' ability to speak.

l: Dorothy, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Dorothy is defended by the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger as the sweetest girl in the world. She tests whether Toto can speak words, learns that he prefers not to, and is delighted when he finally says, "All right. Here I go!" before running away.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Betsy is identified by Hank as his beloved little mistress and is welcomed as a friend by the animals. She is amazed that animals in Oz can talk, enjoys herself greatly in Oz, and wishes that every child could live there.

l: Toto, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Toto is a shaggy black dog who understands everything said to him but prefers not to speak. He communicates with barks and his tail, then says, "All right. Here I go!" when Dorothy asks him to prove he can use words.

l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: The Land of Oz enables Hank to speak after he enters it, and most animals there can talk. It is presented as a place of friendship, beautiful gardens, fountains, and abundant flowers.

l: Land of Love, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: The Land of Oz is described as a Land of Love in which friendship outranks every other quality. Its inhabitants must be friends in order to retain the love of the land.

l: friendship, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Friendship is declared more important than competing claims about which girl is sweetest. Ozma uses this principle to reconcile Hank, the Sawhorse, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger.

l: love, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Love is shown through the loyalty of Hank to Betsy, the animals' devotion to Dorothy or Ozma, and the welcome extended to friends in Oz. Ozma says that the Land of Oz is a Land of Love and that its inhabitants must be friends to retain its love.

l: animal speech in Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Twenty-Five
s: Animals in Oz generally speak, and Hank begins speaking as soon as he enters the land. Toto is an exception by choice: although the spell lets him speak words and he understands everything said to him, he prefers barks, tail signals, and silence.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: Cap'n Bill and Trot, longtime companions, set out in a small boat to explore caves along the rocky coast. Cap'n Bill notices ominous stillness in the hot afternoon but agrees to continue. A Great Whirlpool draws their boat into its circular current, and despite Cap'n Bill's efforts, they are carried toward the dark hole at its center. Both remain brave as they face the danger.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: Cap'n Bill is a former sailor who lost his left leg below the knee and now lives with Trot's mother as a star boarder. He teaches and accompanies Trot, rows their boat, and recognizes the signs of dangerous weather. When the Great Whirlpool catches them, he rows with all his strength, but the left oar breaks and he finally puts an arm around Trot to shield her.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: Trot is a very little girl with solemn eyes and an earnest, simple manner, and Cap'n Bill has taught her almost everything she knows. She steers the boat while Cap'n Bill rows and remains silent and brave as the Great Whirlpool draws them toward its center.

l: whirlpool, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: The Great Whirlpool forms when a whirl in the air creates a powerful swirl in the water. It makes the ocean slope downward into a basin with a large hole at the center, drawing the boat around its edge and toward the hole.

l: the ocean, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: The ocean is blue and glassy beneath the acacia tree and becomes dangerously still during the hot afternoon. Near the Great Whirlpool, its surface is drawn into a rapidly rotating basin with walls of water surrounding a dark central hole.

l: the boat, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter One
s: The boat belongs to Cap'n Bill and is moored to a rock by a stout cable before Cap'n Bill and Trot take it toward the caves. The Great Whirlpool catches the boat, carries it around the circular basin, and pulls it progressively closer to the central hole despite Cap'n Bill's efforts to escape.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill are swept from their boat into the ocean and carried underwater to a cavern beneath the sea. They explore the cavern, find a dark hole that may be their only escape, and struggle with the danger of starvation and thirst. Cap'n Bill catches and cooks a fish, but they know they cannot remain in the cavern indefinitely without drinking water. The next morning, a huge strange winged creature emerges from the pool and frightens them.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Trot survives the underwater journey with Cap'n Bill and reaches a sandy beach inside a cavern. She helps Cap'n Bill recover, explores the cavern with him, and argues that they should investigate the dark hole because staying there will eventually cause them to starve. She eats cooked fish, worries about their supply of drinking water, and sees the strange winged creature emerge from the pool.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Cap'n Bill is separated from the boat and carried underwater with Trot to the cavern. He examines their surroundings, hesitates to enter the dark hole, catches a fish with crab bait, and cooks it over a seaweed fire. He knows that remaining in the cavern will lead to death, but he dislikes the idea of entering the unknown passage.

l: the ocean, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The ocean carries Trot and Cap'n Bill downward through the hole and later draws them in a slanting direction through still, cool depths. The cavern's pool appears to be connected to the large ocean.

l: the cavern under the sea, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The cavern is a warm, lonely, dome-like place with rugged rocks, a sandy beach, a pool of water, and a soft bluish-green glow. Trot and Cap'n Bill reach it after their underwater fall and remain there while their clothes dry, they cook a fish, and they sleep. The cavern has plentiful seaweed but no visible outside entrance, and staying there would eventually leave them without food or water.

l: the pool, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The pool is at the foot of the cavern's sandy beach and apparently leads into the ocean. Cap'n Bill fishes in it and eventually catches a silver-scaled fish. The strange winged creature later emerges from the pool.

l: the dark hole, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The dark hole is a round opening at the rear of the cavern. It is the only possible way Trot and Cap'n Bill can find an exit, but Cap'n Bill fears it may lead to a place worse than the cavern, so they do not enter it in this unit.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The strange winged creature emerges from the pool the morning after Trot and Cap'n Bill arrive. It is neither clearly a fish nor a beast, has four legs, tough-skinned wings, a parrot-like head and beak, and a scarlet crest of wavy plumes. It is as large as Cap'n Bill and causes both of them to stare in wonder and fear.

l: the underwater journey, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill plunge from the boat into the murky ocean depths, fall rapidly, and then descend more slowly as unseen arms seem to support them. After reaching a great depth, they are drawn upward and sideways through still water before surfacing in the cavern's pool and being cast onto its sandy beach.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill meet an Ork named Flipper, who has escaped a whirlpool and a submerged cavern with the help of mermaids. The Ork explains that he comes from Orkland, can fly with small wings and a propeller-like tail, and carries Cap'n Bill and Trot across a vast underground gulf. The three enter a long tunnel, but their candles and food steadily run out as they travel for hours. They stop to sleep in the tunnel after the Ork's feet become painfully sore from walking.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Trot meets the Ork and learns about his escape from the whirlpool and his origins in Orkland. She rides on the Ork's back across the underground cavern, then walks with Cap'n Bill through the seemingly endless tunnel. She becomes tired and hungry but remains brave.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Cap'n Bill shares food with the Ork and uses candles to guide the group through the tunnel and across the cavern. He rides first on the Ork's back, helps Trot cross safely, and worries about their dwindling candles and provisions. After walking all day on his wooden leg, he sleeps in the tunnel with Trot and the Ork.

l: Flipper, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Flipper is the Ork's name, given in his account of leaving home to see the world. His father warned him about dangerous Men, but Flipper's curiosity led him to travel far from Orkland and lose track of his way home.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Ork introduces himself as a harmless, intelligent creature named Flipper. He says Orks rule all living things in Orkland, and he can fly using four small wings and a propeller-like tail. He explores the gulf below the tunnel, carries Cap'n Bill and Trot to a distant passage, and guides them through the tunnel, though walking causes severe pain in his feet.

l: whirlpool, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The whirlpool captures the Ork when he flies too close and its air suction pulls him into the ocean depths. It also carries Trot and Cap'n Bill into the cavern where they meet the Ork.

l: the cavern under the sea, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The cavern serves as a prison for Trot and Cap'n Bill after the whirlpool casts them there, and the Ork reaches it after swimming upward from another submerged cavern. It contains a sloping passage leading to a black hole and a precipice above a deep lake.

l: tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The tunnel begins beyond a narrow hole in the cavern and eventually opens into a large passage beyond a dangerous underground gulf. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork walk through it for hours without finding a change in their surroundings, using candles while their food and light supplies diminish.

l: the Ork's flight, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Ork's propeller-like tail and small wings allow it to fly swiftly and carry passengers. It flies down into the gulf to investigate, then transports Cap'n Bill and Trot separately to the distant tunnel, making the journey safely and quickly.

l: the Ork's escape from the whirlpool, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: After the whirlpool pulls the Ork into the ocean, mermaids rescue him and drag him into a cavern. He remains there overnight, then dives into the water and swims upward and onward until he reaches the cavern where Trot and Cap'n Bill are staying.

l: the exploration of the tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Ork first discovers the opening to the tunnel and encourages Trot and Cap'n Bill to investigate it. Later, after the group reaches a precipice, he flies down to find a black lake and a tunnel continuing on the left. He then walks ahead through the passage to check for danger while the others follow.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the Ork finish their journey through the tunnel and emerge into daylight at the bottom of a deep shaft. The Ork uses its mechanical propeller tail to fly all three of them out of the shaft and into a beautiful but apparently uninhabited island. They find abundant food and water, including melons, cherries, plums, and nuts, then explore the forest and confirm that the land is surrounded by ocean. At the forest's edge, Trot and Cap'n Bill discover a shed-like house and go to investigate it.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Cap'n Bill wakes Trot, helps follow the tunnel, and is relieved when the group reaches the surface. He hangs onto the Ork's rear legs during the flight from the shaft, lands with a shock, and helps find and cut open a melon. He worries that the land is an island but suggests building a raft or boat if necessary, then goes with Trot to investigate the house.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Trot wakes refreshed and eagerly continues through the tunnel with Cap'n Bill and the Ork. She rides across the Ork's shoulders during the flight from the shaft, is delighted by the melon, and helps explore the island. She is relieved to be above ground but worries that being on an island may make them prisoners, and she spots the house near the forest.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The Ork recognizes that the tunnel is nearing its end and uses its mechanical propeller tail to carry Trot and Cap'n Bill out of the shaft. After landing, it helps determine that the surrounding land may be an island, eats melon, and flies over the forest because its feet are sore and lumpy from walking on rocks.

l: tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The tunnel narrows and turns sharply before ending at a rocky shaft where daylight is visible from above. Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the Ork complete their passage through it after traveling for a long time.

l: shaft, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The shaft is a deep, rocky, straight-up well with its top far above the travelers. The Ork carries Trot and Cap'n Bill from its bottom to the surface, despite bumping against its rough sides.

l: daylight, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Daylight reaches the travelers through the top of the shaft after they make two turns in the passage. It grows brighter as the Ork flies upward and finally gives way to clear air and sunshine.

l: Earth, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The Ork says that anything above ground on Earth is better than the best things underground. Trot calls Earth a beautiful place when they emerge among trees, shrubs, flowers, and green turf.

l: the ocean, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The Ork sees or thinks it sees the ocean from the landing place and flies to a nearby hill to check. From the hill, Cap'n Bill and Trot see blue waves in front of them and on both sides, and they later reach the ocean shore beyond the forest.

l: island (the island previously visited), The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The land appears to be an island because ocean surrounds it on three sides from the hill and lies beyond the forest. Trot worries that they may be prisoners there, while Cap'n Bill considers building a raft or boat to leave if needed.

l: the forest, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: A forest lies behind the hill and blocks the view in that direction. It consists entirely of nut trees, including walnuts, filberts, almonds, and chestnuts, and Cap'n Bill and Trot walk through it to reach the ocean shore.

l: melons, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Melons grow among tangled vines on the island. Cap'n Bill cuts one open, confirms that it is ripe and safe, and shares it with Trot and the Ork; many more melons are found, providing abundant food and water.

l: house, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: At the edge of the forest, Trot notices a shed-like structure that appears to be a house. Cap'n Bill agrees that it is a building, and they go to see whether it is occupied.

l: the exploration of the tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The journey through the tunnel lasts through the night, and Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the Ork resume it after sleeping. They pass through narrow, sharply turning passages before reaching the end and finding the shaft.

l: Ork's flight from the shaft, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: During the Ork's flight from the shaft, Trot sits across its shoulders while Cap'n Bill grips its rear legs. The Ork's propeller tail lifts them up the long shaft, though it bumps against the rough walls several times, and it eventually lands gently in the sunshine.

l: food and water, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The explorers find melons, cherries, wild plums, walnuts, filberts, almonds, and chestnuts. Cap'n Bill explains that melons provide both food and water, and Trot concludes that they are unlikely to starve even if the land is an island.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill meet Pessim, the quarrelsome Observer and self-proclaimed King of his own island, where they also reunite with the Ork after it has been shrunk by eating a lavender berry. Pessim explains that a deep purple berry reverses the lavender berry's effect, allowing the Ork to regain its natural size. After living unhappily on the island for several days, Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork devise a plan to escape by shrinking Trot and Cap'n Bill and carrying them in Trot's sunbonnet. They set off over the ocean with Trot and Cap'n Bill in the sunbonnet tied around the Ork's neck.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Trot meets Pessim and is troubled by his rudeness and constant fault-finding. She helps the Ork regain its natural size with a deep purple berry and agrees to shrink herself so the Ork can carry her and Cap'n Bill away from the island. After eating a lavender berry, she becomes tiny and rides in her sunbonnet with the berries needed to restore her size.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Cap'n Bill politely questions Pessim but soon recognizes that the little man is unpleasant and that his neighbors were right to leave him on the island. He helps gather the magic berries and accepts the plan to shrink himself so the Ork can carry him. After eating a lavender berry, he becomes tiny, including his wooden leg, and climbs awkwardly into Trot's sunbonnet.

l: Pessim, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Pessim calls himself the Observer and is the self-proclaimed King of the island, but he continually complains about everything, including the trees, rocks, sand, water, weather, and his visitors. He reveals that his neighbors brought him to the island because he was quarrelsome and fault-finding, and that he once became tiny after eating a lavender berry before returning to normal by eating a deep purple berry. He helps tie Trot's sunbonnet around the Ork's neck, although he predicts that the travelers will be drowned or crushed.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The Ork arrives in a tiny form after eating a lavender berry and tells Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Pessim how it was affected. It regains its natural size by eating a deep purple berry and then suggests using the same berries to shrink Trot and Cap'n Bill for transport. The Ork carries them away from the island in Trot's sunbonnet tied around its neck.

l: Pessim's island, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Pessim's island has a grove, an ocean shore, trees bearing unusual fruits, and no other land visible nearby. Pessim considers it his exclusive property, but Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork remain there for three unhappy days because they cannot otherwise leave. The island contains both lavender berries that cause shrinking and deep purple berries that restore normal size.

l: shed (Pessim's island), The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The shed is an open shelter made from a roof of boughs and branches fastened to the sides, facing the sea. Trot and Cap'n Bill take refuge there from the rain, and they later make beds of leaves inside it while Pessim sleeps in a hammock between two trees. The shed has no furniture except Pessim's stool, which he calls his throne.

l: lavender berries, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The lavender berry is a small, lovely lavender-colored fruit that causes whoever eats it to shrink dramatically. The Ork and Pessim both become tiny after eating one, and later Trot and Cap'n Bill eat lavender berries so the Ork can carry them.

l: purple berries, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The deep purple berry is the antidote to the lavender berry. Pessim ate one after shrinking and returned to his former size, and the Ork also regained its natural size after eating one. Cap'n Bill gathers six deep purple berries to take along for restoring Trot and himself after their journey.

l: Trot's sunbonnet, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Trot's sunbonnet serves as a makeshift bag because it is hollow in the middle and has two strings. It holds tiny Trot and Cap'n Bill, along with the deep purple berries, and is tied around the Ork's neck so the Ork can carry them.

l: shrinking and regrowing through the berries, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Eating a lavender berry causes a person or creature to shrink, while eating a deep purple berry causes it to grow back to its former size. The Ork and Pessim demonstrate the effects first, and Trot and Cap'n Bill use the same process as part of their escape plan.

l: escape from the island, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork cannot find another practical way to leave the island, and Cap'n Bill lacks tools to build a raft. They therefore plan for Trot and Cap'n Bill to eat lavender berries, ride in Trot's sunbonnet, and later eat deep purple berries to regain their size. The Ork carries them over the ocean after Pessim ties the sunbonnet around its neck.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: Cap'n Bill and Trot, reduced to midget size, travel for hours in a sunbonnet carried by the Ork over a large ocean. The Ork finds an unfamiliar land, lands on a mountain peak, and helps them leave the sunbonnet. Cap'n Bill and Trot eat purple berries and return to their natural size. Cap'n Bill stores three remaining berries in a wooden box before they begin examining the unnamed country.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: Cap'n Bill travels with Trot in the sunbonnet while the Ork carries them over the ocean. He cuts a slit in the sunbonnet so they can escape, eats a purple berry, returns to his natural size, and stores three remaining berries in a wooden box.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: Trot travels with Cap'n Bill in the sunbonnet and remains awake during much of the flight. She worries about reaching a country inhabited only by Orks, helps preserve the purple berries, eats one, and regains her natural size.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The Ork carries Cap'n Bill and Trot in the sunbonnet over the ocean, flying steadily in a straight line while searching for land. It finds an unfamiliar country, lands on a mountain peak, and struggles to untie the sunbonnet because its claws cannot easily reach the strings.

l: the midgets, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The midgets are Cap'n Bill and Trot while they are reduced in size. They travel in the sunbonnet over the ocean, leave it after landing, and regain their natural size by eating purple berries.

l: the Flight of the Midgets, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The Flight of the Midgets is the journey of Cap'n Bill and Trot in the sunbonnet as the Ork carries them for hours over the ocean toward unknown land. It ends when the Ork lands on a mountain peak in an unfamiliar country.

l: Trot's sunbonnet, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The sunbonnet carries Cap'n Bill and Trot during the Ork's long flight. Cap'n Bill cuts a slit in it so they can get out, and Trot picks it up after returning to her natural size.

l: purple berries, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The purple berries restore Cap'n Bill and Trot to their natural size when they eat them. Trot protects two berries during the flight, and Cap'n Bill places three sound berries in a wooden box after discarding one that was badly jammed.

l: the ocean, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The ocean lies below the Ork's long flight and is described as large. The Ork searches its horizon for land before finding a small island and then a much larger landmass.

l: unnamed country, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Six
s: The unnamed country is reached after the Ork flies over the ocean and lands on a mountain peak. The Ork has never seen it before and describes it as containing mountains, deserts, green valleys, queer cities, lakes, and rivers.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork reach the top of a mountain in the Land of Mo and enter a stone house. They meet the Bumpy Man, who calls himself the Mountain Ear and says he listens to nature's sounds to keep the mountain from quaking or spouting. Their host serves them hot molasses candy and lemonade, explaining that Mo has no water and that it rains lemonade. The travelers sleep before the fire while the Mountain Ear remains alert and listens through the night.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: Trot climbs the mountain with Cap'n Bill and the Ork and enters the Bumpy Man's house. She learns that they are in the Land of Mo, eats and pulls hot molasses candy, drinks lemonade, and sleeps before the fire.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: Cap'n Bill climbs the mountain with Trot and knocks on the Bumpy Man's door. He asks what country they are in, eats some molasses candy and drinks lemonade, and then sleeps before the fire.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The Ork flies to the top of the mountain to investigate and calls for Trot and Cap'n Bill to join him. He explains that he has traveled widely while searching for his home, eats some molasses candy, refuses the lemonade, and says that water is necessary for life.

l: Bumpy Man, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The Bumpy Man welcomes the travelers into his stone house, prepares hot molasses candy, and gives them lemonade. He says his bumps predict the weather and warns that a snowstorm is coming, then keeps the fire burning while the travelers sleep.

l: Mountain Ear, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The Bumpy Man is known throughout the Land of Mo as the Mountain Ear. He listens to sounds made by nature and tells the mountain about blizzards, rain, and snow so that it will remain steady and not quake or spout.

l: Land of Mo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The Land of Mo is the country where Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork arrive. It has mountains, valleys, hills, houses, and people or animals, but no water; instead, it rains lemonade.

l: mountain, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The mountain has grassy slopes, bushes, slender trees, tumbled rocks, and a broad, level top. A house stands at its center, and the Mountain Ear believes that listening to natural sounds keeps the mountain from becoming frightened, quaking, or spouting.

l: house (on the mountain), The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: The house on the mountain is a neatly constructed stone building with one large, simply furnished room. It contains stone benches, a stone table, a stone fireplace, and a chimney from which smoke is rising.

l: molasses candy, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Seven
s: Molasses candy is served hot from a bubbling kettle in the Bumpy Man's house. Trot lets it cool, pulls it with her hands, and finds that it pulls beautifully; Cap'n Bill and the Ork eat some, while the Bumpy Man refuses to try it.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, the Ork, and the Bumpy Man find Button-Bright buried safely in Mo snow, which is warm, buttered popcorn. Cap'n Bill captures three birds and uses purple berries to enlarge them so they can carry the travelers. He makes swings from strips of the Bumpy Man's old clothes, and the travelers begin following the Ork toward a sandy desert. The group plans to discover what lies beyond the desert by flying across it.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Trot learns that Mo snow is warm popcorn and recognizes Button-Bright when he is rescued. She travels with him, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork, admires the beautiful birds, and flies in a swing attached to one of the enlarged birds.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Cap'n Bill helps pull Button-Bright from the popcorn snow and captures birds by tying cords around their legs. He feeds purple berries to three birds, enlarging them enough to carry the travelers, and makes swings for the journey from strips of the Bumpy Man's old clothes.

l: Bumpy Man, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The Bumpy Man explains that winter has arrived and that Mo snow is popcorn. He shovels a path, helps uncover Button-Bright, provides hospitality, and gives Cap'n Bill an old gray suit to use in making swings.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Button-Bright is found buried in a bank of popcorn snow, calmly eating the popcorn and asking for his cap. He says that he has lost his Magic Umbrella and therefore has no home, and he joins Trot and the others on their flight.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The Ork is surprised that the birds are covered with feathers and later helps plan the travelers' escape from the mountain. It leads the three enlarged birds and the other travelers toward the sandy desert.

l: the three enlarged birds, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Three young cousin birds volunteer to carry the travelers. After eating purple berries, they grow to nearly the size of full-grown ostriches and carry the travelers in swings while following the Ork.

l: Land of Mo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The Land of Mo has warm popcorn snow, talking and educated birds, perfumed winds, and magic berries. Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, and the Ork leave its mountain region to search for another country.

l: the great sandy desert, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The sandy desert lies beyond the mountain in the direction chosen by the Ork. The travelers decide to fly over it to discover what lies beyond.

l: Mo snow, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Mo snow falls in large flakes and is revealed to be crisp, warm, salted, and buttered popcorn. It buries Button-Bright but also keeps him warm and supplied with food until he is uncovered.

l: purple berries, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Cap'n Bill still has three purple berries in his wooden box. He gives one to each of three birds, and the berries cause the birds to grow much larger.

l: the birds' enlargement, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The birds' enlargement makes them much larger than the Ork and nearly as large as full-grown ostriches. Their new size allows them to carry the travelers in swings.

l: the rescue of Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The Bumpy Man discovers a pair of feet beneath a deep bank of Mo snow. He and Cap'n Bill pull out Button-Bright, who is alive, unharmed, and eating popcorn.

l: the Flight of the Midgets, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The travelers begin a flight across the sandy desert after deciding to follow the Ork. The Ork leads while the three enlarged birds carry Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright.

l: the birds' swings, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: Cap'n Bill makes swings by cutting the Bumpy Man's old gray clothes into strips and twisting them into strong cords. He attaches one swing beneath each enlarged bird, and Button-Bright tests one before the journey begins.

l: the purple berries' size-changing power, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eight
s: The purple berries can rapidly increase the size of living creatures. When three birds eat them, the birds grow from eagle-sized to nearly the size of full-grown ostriches.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, the Ork, and three birds cross the great sandy desert and enter the beautiful country of Jinxland. The Ork leaves to search for Orkland, while the birds return to the Land of Mo, leaving the three travelers to continue on foot. A woman tells them that Jinxland is part of the Quadling Country in the Land of Oz but is ruled by its own King, Krewl, because the surrounding mountains cannot be crossed. After receiving food from the woman, the travelers head toward King Krewl's castle and hear someone sobbing in the nearby grove.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Trot rides comfortably in a swing carried by a large bird during the flight over the great sandy desert. In Jinxland, she admires the country, questions the woman about its King, eats the food the woman provides, and continues toward King Krewl's castle with Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Cap'n Bill travels in a swing carried by one of the birds and remains confident in the ropes he fastened. He asks the woman about the country, learns about King Krewl and Jinxland's separation from the rest of the Quadling Country, and leads the travelers toward the castle.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Button-Bright follows Trot during the flight and says he is not thinking because thinking tires him. He eats heartily, fills his pockets with cakes and cheese, comments on Jinxland and Ozma, and walks with the others toward King Krewl's castle.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: The Ork leads the flight into the country beyond the great sandy desert. It leaves the travelers to search for its home on the other side of the desert, promising to return in a week if it does not find Orkland.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Jinxland is a beautiful country with forests, hills, fields, fountains, rivers, lakes, houses, castles, and palaces. It lies in the Quadling Country of the Land of Oz but is separated from the rest of the Quadling Country by impassable mountains and is ruled by its own King.

l: Land of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: The woman explains that every bit of land surrounded by the great desert is part of the Land of Oz. Jinxland is in its Quadling Country, although its people live separately from the rest of the Quadling Country and are not ruled there by Ozma of Oz.

l: the great sandy desert, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: The great sandy desert is broad, monotonous, and filled with deadly fumes and gases near the ground. The travelers cross it by flying high above it, and the Ork intends to search for Orkland on its other side.

l: mountains, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: The row of high mountains separates Jinxland from the rest of the Quadling Country. Its sides are so steep that the woman says no one can cross it, leaving Jinxland isolated from Ozma's rule.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: King Krewl rules Jinxland and punishes his subjects severely for treason. The woman is afraid to discuss him and says that people are safer when they know less about his actions; he hunts with fierce courtiers and war captains when he is away from his castle.

l: the King's castle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: King Krewl's castle is a splendid structure whose towers rise above the surrounding trees. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright walk toward it after learning that it belongs to King Krewl.

l: the Flight of the Midgets, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Nine
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright fly into Jinxland in swings carried by three birds, following the Ork over the great sandy desert and through a pink-tinted mist. They land near the desert's edge, while the Ork continues on alone and the three birds later return toward the Land of Mo.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Button-Bright, Trot, and Cap'n Bill meet Pon, the gardener's boy, who is grieving because Princess Gloria loves him but King Krewl opposes their relationship. Pon explains that Gloria is Krewl's niece and that Krewl is forcing her to marry the wealthy, elderly courtier Googly-Goo. Pon reveals that he is actually the son of King Phearse, whom Krewl trapped beneath stones in a deep pond, making Pon the rightful prince of Jinxland. After hearing Pon's story and learning that the King's guards beat him, Trot and Cap'n Bill promise to speak favorably of him if they get the chance to meet King Krewl.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Button-Bright discovers Pon sobbing beneath a tree and asks why he does not get another heart. He listens to Pon's story and advises him to get his broken heart fixed.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Trot sympathetically asks Pon to tell his troubles and is indignant when she hears how King Krewl treated him and Princess Gloria. She asks about Gloria's father and observes that Gloria would be Queen of Jinxland if she had her rights.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Cap'n Bill questions Pon's account and initially suggests that King Krewl may believe a royal Princess should not marry a gardener's boy. After hearing Pon's history, he agrees to put in a good word for Pon if he gets the chance to speak with King Krewl.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Pon, the gardener's boy, tells Trot and Cap'n Bill that Princess Gloria loves him and that King Krewl is preventing them from marrying. He reveals that he is the son of King Phearse, the former King of Jinxland, whom Krewl trapped beneath stones in a deep pond, and therefore considers himself the rightful prince. Pon also describes being beaten by two of Krewl's guards while Gloria watched.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Princess Gloria is described as the niece of King Krewl and the loveliest and sweetest maiden in Jinxland. She loves Pon, has refused Googly-Goo thirty-nine times, and has told Pon that she will marry only him.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: King Krewl is Princess Gloria's guardian and has commanded her to marry Googly-Goo. He struck and kicked Pon, dragged Gloria into the castle, and later held her back while his guards beat Pon. Pon also says that Krewl trapped King Phearse beneath stones in a deep pond and took the throne of Jinxland.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Jinxland is ruled by King Krewl, although Pon claims he is the rightful prince because he is the son of the former King Phearse. Princess Gloria would be Queen of Jinxland if she had her rights, according to Trot.

l: the King's castle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Princess Gloria lives in King Krewl's castle. After striking Pon, King Krewl dragged Gloria into the castle.

l: Princess Gloria's love for Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Princess Gloria falls in love with Pon while he works in the gardens and tells him that he has touched her heart as no other young man has. She continues to meet him and assures him that she will wed only him.

l: the proposed marriage of Gloria and Googly-Goo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: King Krewl wants Princess Gloria to marry the wealthy courtier Googly-Goo, who is old enough to be her father. Gloria has refused Googly-Goo thirty-nine times, but he continues to pursue her with rich presents for the King.

l: Pon's beating, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Ten
s: Two of King Krewl's guards seize Pon in the grape arbor and beat him terribly while Princess Gloria watches. King Krewl holds Gloria back so that she cannot interfere, and Pon says the beating helped break his heart.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright enter King Krewl's castle in Jinxland and are treated as potentially magical strangers. They learn that Lord Googly-Goo wants to marry Princess Gloria, who loves Pon, and that King Krewl is considering how to destroy her love for Pon. King Krewl and Googly-Goo summon the Wicked Witch to test whether Cap'n Bill is a magician. After finding Gloria with Pon, King Krewl locks her in a room and prepares to meet the Wicked Witch.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Cap'n Bill leads Trot and Button-Bright into King Krewl's castle and boldly speaks to the King, requesting rooms and a banquet. King Krewl and Lord Googly-Goo suspect that he may possess magical powers because he crossed the desert, and they summon the Wicked Witch to test him.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Trot enters King Krewl's castle with Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright and is uneasy about the King and the possibility that their food may be poisoned. She dislikes Lord Googly-Goo and feels sorry for Princess Gloria.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Button-Bright enters the castle with Cap'n Bill and Trot and is seated in a room between theirs. He observes that King Krewl intends to sell Princess Gloria for the jewels promised by Lord Googly-Goo.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: King Krewl receives Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright as strangers and becomes wary of Cap'n Bill's apparent magical powers. He discusses destroying Gloria's love for Pon, locks Gloria in a room after finding her with Pon, and summons the Wicked Witch to examine Cap'n Bill.

l: Googly-Goo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Lord Googly-Goo wants to marry Princess Gloria and offers King Krewl a bushel and a half of precious jewels if the marriage occurs. He suggests testing Cap'n Bill with the Wicked Witch and becomes furious when he finds Gloria with Pon.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Princess Gloria refuses to marry Lord Googly-Goo because she loves Pon. King Krewl finds her with Pon, drags her back to the castle, and locks her in a lower-floor room.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Pon is the gardener's boy whom Princess Gloria loves. He kneels before Gloria in the garden but escapes by climbing a ladder over the wall when King Krewl approaches.

l: Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: The Wicked Witch is summoned by King Krewl at Lord Googly-Goo's suggestion. She is expected to determine whether Cap'n Bill is a common man or a magician.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Jinxland is described as a hidden country reached by crossing a deadly desert. Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright arrive there as the first strangers known to have entered the country.

l: the King's castle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: King Krewl's castle is a large, richly furnished building with winding decorated passages, a central courtyard, and rooms that separate the three visitors. Gloria is locked in one of its lower-floor rooms.

l: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill's arrival in Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: The arrival concerns Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright, who enter Jinxland after crossing the desert. King Krewl gives them rooms and a banquet but later views them, especially Cap'n Bill, with suspicion.

l: Gloria's imprisonment, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Gloria's imprisonment begins after King Krewl catches her with Pon in the rear garden. He drags her into the castle, pushes her into a lower-floor room, and locks the door.

l: Princess Gloria's love for Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Gloria's love for Pon prevents her from accepting Lord Googly-Goo's marriage proposal. King Krewl and Googly-Goo discuss killing or destroying that love, but no method is carried out in this unit.

l: the proposed marriage of Gloria and Googly-Goo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Eleven
s: Gloria has repeatedly refused to marry Googly-Goo. Googly-Goo offers precious jewels to King Krewl in connection with the marriage, while King Krewl seeks a way to overcome Gloria's love for Pon.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Trot frees Princess Gloria from her room and learns that Gloria loves Pon and refuses to love Googly-Goo. King Krewl and Googly-Goo enlist Blinkie to freeze Gloria's heart, while Blinkie transforms the sleeping Cap'n Bill into a grasshopper with a wooden leg. The transformed Cap'n Bill escapes through a window, and Trot and Button-Bright are expelled from King Krewl's castle. They find Pon, who shelters them for the night and suspects that Blinkie enchanted Cap'n Bill.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Trot witnesses King Krewl dragging Gloria away, then unlocks Gloria's room and comforts her. After Cap'n Bill disappears, she searches for him, is turned away from the castle, and joins Button-Bright in finding shelter with Pon.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Princess Gloria tells Trot that she loves Pon and will never love Googly-Goo. King Krewl and Googly-Goo plan to have Blinkie freeze her heart so that she can no longer love Pon.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Pon remains loved by Princess Gloria despite opposition from King Krewl and Googly-Goo. He shelters Trot and Button-Bright in his cottage, feeds them, and suspects that Blinkie enchanted Cap'n Bill.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: King Krewl confines Gloria, opposes her love for Pon, and agrees with Googly-Goo to have Blinkie freeze her heart. He helps Blinkie reach the sleeping Cap'n Bill, then orders Trot and Button-Bright barred from his castle.

l: Googly-Goo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Googly-Goo helps King Krewl oppose Gloria's love for Pon and agrees to pay Blinkie for the heart-freezing enchantment. He does not accompany King Krewl and Blinkie to Cap'n Bill's room because he goes home to get the promised money and jewels.

l: Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Blinkie is an old, one-eyed Wicked Witch and the leader of the witches in Jinxland. She agrees to freeze Gloria's heart, then transforms the sleeping Cap'n Bill into a small gray grasshopper with a wooden left leg.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Cap'n Bill falls asleep in the castle after his adventures. Blinkie transforms him into a grasshopper with a wooden leg, and he escapes through the open window before she can strike him.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Button-Bright is found by Trot after both have been turned away from the castle. He helps her search for a place to sleep and goes with her to Pon's cottage, where he eats and sleeps.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: The transformed form of Cap'n Bill is a little gray grasshopper whose last left-leg joint is made of wood. It can speak, threatens Blinkie and King Krewl, and makes a remarkable jump through the window to escape.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Jinxland lies far from the center of Oz and is cut off by steep mountains and a bottomless gulf. Oz's laws are not well obeyed there, and several witches live in the country with King Krewl's permission.

l: the King's castle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: King Krewl's castle contains Gloria's locked room and the room where Cap'n Bill sleeps. Trot and Button-Bright are later forbidden to enter it, and Cap'n Bill leaves it only after being transformed and escaping through a window.

l: love, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Gloria explains that love is decided by the heart rather than by reason or a person's worth. Blinkie says that love is difficult to destroy because it may return, comparing it to cats having nine lives.

l: witchcraft, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Witchcraft is forbidden in the Land of Oz but is practiced in Jinxland, where King Krewl permits witches to use their powers. King Krewl sometimes employs witchcraft for cruelty and revenge and must pay Blinkie money or jewels for enchantments.

l: Gloria's heart-freezing enchantment, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: Blinkie proposes freezing Gloria's heart so that Gloria can no longer love Pon. King Krewl and Googly-Goo accept the plan and arrange for Gloria to be taken to Blinkie's house the next day, but the enchantment has not yet been performed in this unit.

l: Cap'n Bill's transformation into a grasshopper, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Twelve
s: While Cap'n Bill sleeps, Blinkie mixes magical powders and transforms him into a little gray grasshopper with a wooden left leg. The transformation leaves him able to speak and jump, and he escapes before Blinkie can harm him.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Glinda the Good learns from the Great Book of Records that Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill have arrived in Jinxland, where King Krewl and several Wicked Witches threaten them and Princess Gloria. She sends the Scarecrow to protect the three outsiders and gives him magical supplies, including a rope and pills for a spider. The Scarecrow crosses the mountains separating the Quadling Country from Jinxland, crosses the Great Gulf on a spider-silk bridge, and heads toward King Krewl's castle.

l: Glinda, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Glinda lives in a splendid palace in the southernmost part of the Quadling Country and serves as the Royal Sorceress of Oz. She learns about events through the Great Book of Records and sends the Scarecrow to protect Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill in Jinxland.

l: Land of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The Land of Oz includes the Quadling Country and the isolated region of Jinxland. Glinda uses her magic to help the subjects of Ozma's kingdom, while Oz people know little about Jinxland.

l: Scarecrow, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The Scarecrow visits Glinda and agrees to travel to Jinxland to protect Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill. Equipped with magical objects from Glinda, he crosses the mountains and the Great Gulf and walks toward King Krewl's castle.

l: Great Book of Records, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The Great Book of Records records everything that takes place throughout the world as it happens. Glinda uses it to learn that three people from the Outside World have arrived in Jinxland and to follow their troubles.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Jinxland is a small region near the Quadling Country, separated from it by high mountains and a deep gulf. It is ruled by King Krewl, and its people live in fear of him and several Wicked Witches.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: King Krewl rules Jinxland despite having no right to the title. He is described as wicked and fierce, and the people of Jinxland live in constant fear of him.

l: Wicked Witches of Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Several Wicked Witches keep the inhabitants of Jinxland in a state of terror. They understand evil forms of witchcraft, including transforming a sailor and threatening Princess Gloria.

l: Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Blinkie is one of the Wicked Witches of Jinxland. She transforms a respectable old sailor into a grasshopper and plans to freeze Princess Gloria's heart.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Trot is one of the three people from the Outside World who arrive in Jinxland. She and Button-Bright are turned out of King Krewl's castle and find refuge in the hut of Pon, the gardener's boy.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Button-Bright arrives in Jinxland with Trot and Cap'n Bill. He and Trot are turned out of King Krewl's castle and take refuge in Pon's hut; the Scarecrow already knows him from an earlier visit to Oz.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Cap'n Bill is one of the three people from the Outside World who arrive in Jinxland. One of the witches transforms a respectable old sailor into a grasshopper, and Glinda sends the Scarecrow to protect Cap'n Bill along with Trot and Button-Bright.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Princess Gloria is a beautiful girl from Jinxland. Blinkie is planning to freeze her heart.

l: Scarecrow's mission to protect Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Glinda assigns the Scarecrow to travel to Jinxland and protect Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill from the wicked King Krewl and the witches. He begins the mission immediately and reaches the plains of Jinxland.

l: Great Gulf, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The Great Gulf lies at the foot of the mountains separating the Quadling Country from Jinxland and is believed to be impassable. The Scarecrow crosses it using two strong strands spun by a spider after it eats magical pills.

l: mountains, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The mountains separate Jinxland from the Quadling Country and have sides too steep to climb. The Scarecrow crosses them with a magic rope supplied by Glinda.

l: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill's arrival in Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: The Great Book of Records reports that three people from the Outside World have arrived in Jinxland. Trot and Button-Bright are expelled from King Krewl's castle and find shelter with Pon, while the three face danger from the king and the witches.

l: Gloria's heart-freezing enchantment, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
s: Blinkie plans to use witchcraft to freeze Princess Gloria's heart. Glinda learns of the threat through the Great Book of Records and regards the situation as dreadful.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Button-Bright wanders away from Pon's house while eating blackberries and chasing a butterfly, becoming lost again. King Krewl brings Princess Gloria to Blinkie's house, where Blinkie and three summoned witches perform a ceremony that freezes Gloria's heart and removes her ability to love. Pon and Trot witness the ceremony, escape the pursuing witches, and find Gloria, but she rejects Pon and everyone else with cold indifference. Googly-Goo tries to force Gloria to marry him, but she strikes him into a muddy ditch and continues on alone.

l: Button-Bright, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Button-Bright wakes before the others, wanders away from Pon's house while eating blackberries and chasing a butterfly, and becomes lost again. He assumes that someone will eventually find him.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Trot worries when Button-Bright disappears and follows Pon to Blinkie's house, where she watches the witchcraft ceremony. She and Pon flee the pursuing witches, find Princess Gloria, and later decide to search for Button-Bright and Cap'n Bill.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Pon follows King Krewl and the soldiers because he fears they intend to harm Gloria, then watches Blinkie freeze her heart. He tries to approach Gloria afterward, but she rejects him, so he joins Trot in searching for their friends.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Princess Gloria is taken by King Krewl to Blinkie's house and bound while the witches perform their ceremony. After her heart is frozen, she can no longer love Pon, Googly-Goo, King Krewl, or even herself, and she rejects them all with cold dignity.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: King Krewl escorts Princess Gloria to Blinkie's house and pays Blinkie with money and jewels to freeze Gloria's heart. He threatens to burn Blinkie at the stake if the witch fails, then leaves before the ceremony is completed.

l: Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Blinkie welcomes Gloria to her house and performs the heart-freezing ceremony after receiving payment from King Krewl. She summons three other witches, rejoices when the spell succeeds, and pursues Pon and Trot after they spy on the ceremony.

l: Googly-Goo, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Googly-Goo runs after Gloria and insists that she marry him because he paid for her heart to be frozen and paid King Krewl to permit their marriage. When Gloria refuses, he tries to restrain her, but she strikes him into a muddy ditch.

l: the witches summoned by Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Three witches appear from flashes produced by Blinkie's kettle and temporarily transform themselves into beautiful maidens through witchcraft. They help perform the ceremony, then return to their ugly forms and pursue Pon and Trot by flying on canes or broomsticks.

l: Blinkie's house, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Blinkie's house has eight sides, with a door and a window in each side, and smoke coming from its chimney. It is where Gloria is bound and where Blinkie and the other witches conduct the ceremony.

l: the witchcraft ceremony, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: During the ceremony, Blinkie and three other witches add magical substances to a kettle, chant over it, and dance around Gloria. Blinkie finally throws a ladleful of the mixture onto Gloria's breast, successfully freezing her heart.

l: Gloria's frozen heart, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: Gloria's heart changes from vivid red to gray and then white as frost and icicles form around it. Afterward, Gloria is unable to feel mortal love and responds to Pon, Trot, and Googly-Goo with coldness or rejection.

l: the magical kettle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
s: The magical kettle hangs over a fire and flashes three times, causing another witch to appear with each flash. It bubbles and smokes violently after Blinkie adds another substance, then holds the completed mixture that is used to freeze Gloria's heart.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Trot and Pon search Jinxland for Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright until they meet the Scarecrow, who comes from Oz to help them. Blinkie attacks the Scarecrow, pulls the straw from his body, and then resumes chasing Trot and Pon. The Scarecrow is restuffed, and Cap'n Bill reveals that Blinkie has transformed him into a gray grasshopper with a wooden leg. The Scarecrow explains that Glinda may be able to break the enchantment affecting Cap'n Bill and that she sent him to help the strangers in danger.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Trot searches through Jinxland with Pon for Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright. She meets the Scarecrow, helps restuff him after Blinkie destroys his body, and recognizes Cap'n Bill when he reveals himself as a grasshopper.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Pon searches Jinxland with Trot and is pursued by Blinkie. He helps Trot restuff the Scarecrow and again appeals to Princess Gloria, who remains unable to love because the Wicked Witch has frozen her heart.

l: Scarecrow, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: The Scarecrow comes from the Quadling Country to help Trot and Pon, relying on his highly intelligent brains. He confronts Blinkie, who pulls the straw from his body, but Trot and Pon later restuff him. He explains that Glinda may be able to undo Cap'n Bill's enchantment and that she sent him to help the strangers in danger.

l: Blinkie, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Blinkie traces Trot and Pon to a cornfield and chases them with a stick. She knocks the Scarecrow down, pulls the straw from his body, and then continues pursuing Trot and Pon without noticing that they have hidden from her.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Cap'n Bill has been transformed by Blinkie into a small gray grasshopper with a wooden leg. He reveals his identity to Trot after the Scarecrow has been restuffed and says that the transformation is inconvenient and humiliating but not painful.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Princess Gloria encounters the Scarecrow's talking head and the grasshopper. She says that she does not love Pon or anyone else because the Wicked Witch has frozen her heart, and she declines to restuff the Scarecrow before Trot and Pon arrive.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Fifteen
s: Jinxland is the country where Trot and Pon search through forests, fields, and villages for Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright. The Scarecrow comes there from the Quadling Country because the strangers are in danger from the cruel King and the Wicked Witch.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: The Scarecrow convenes a council of war with Princess Gloria, Pon, Trot, and the grasshopper to plan the conquest of Jinxland and the removal of King Krewl. He declares that Gloria is the rightful heir to the throne and sends Pon to summon King Krewl to surrender. King Krewl refuses and beats Pon with his golden staff. The Scarecrow then sets out alone for the King's castle, intending to conquer Krewl with a borrowed riding-whip.

l: Scarecrow, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: The Scarecrow leads a council of war and declares that the group will conquer King Krewl and place Princess Gloria on the throne of Jinxland. He sends Pon to ask Krewl to surrender, then decides to go to the King's castle himself after Pon is beaten. He says that weapons and blows cannot injure him because he has no nerves, though he does not explain the one exception.

l: Princess Gloria, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: Princess Gloria joins the council but remains cold and reserved. The Scarecrow declares that she is the rightful person to sit upon the throne of Jinxland, and he plans to make her Queen. She shows no apparent reaction when Pon returns injured after being beaten by King Krewl.

l: Pon, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: Pon participates in the council and is sent to King Krewl as a messenger to request his surrender. He enters the King's castle and delivers the summons to surrender to the Scarecrow, but Krewl beats him with a golden staff. Pon returns to the others sore, aching, and sobbing.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: Trot takes part in the council of war and asks how the group will force King Krewl to give up the throne. She feels sorry for Pon after Krewl beats him and questions the Scarecrow about his ability to withstand injury.

l: King Krewl, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: King Krewl is described as a usurper who has no right to rule Jinxland. When Pon summons him to surrender to the Scarecrow, Krewl refuses and beats Pon with his golden staff.

l: Army of Conquest, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: The Scarecrow becomes the acknowledged head of the Army of Conquest. He directs its first action as sending Pon to demand King Krewl's surrender.

l: Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: Jinxland is ruled by King Krewl, whom the Scarecrow identifies as a usurper. The group plans to conquer the Kingdom and place Princess Gloria on its throne.

l: the King's castle, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: Pon enters the King's castle and passes into an enclosed court where King Krewl is seated with his courtiers. After Pon delivers the summons, Krewl has soldiers hold him while he beats him, and Pon then escapes from the castle.

l: throne of Jinxland, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: The Scarecrow says that Princess Gloria alone is entitled to sit upon the throne of Jinxland. He plans to conquer King Krewl and place Gloria on it as Queen.

l: council of war, The Scarecrow of Oz, Chapter Sixteen
s: The Scarecrow calls a council of war with the group to decide what should be done about King Krewl. The council concludes that Pon should politely but firmly summon Krewl to surrender.
